compiled_state.description:
## Problem

Discovered during the Step-7 sibling sweep of baldish-regainable-steed (e4a6-545b-36af-456d), which fixed the tickets-branch CAS push to back off with JITTER (not lockstep) before re-fetching.

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py` publishes the last-pass witness under a 3-attempt CAS loop:

```python
for attempt in range(3):
    if ref_lock._cas_advance(repo_root, LAST_PASS_REF, new_oid=new_oid, old_oid=old_oid, remote=remote):
        ...
        return record
    if attempt == 2:
        break
    sleeper((0.1, 0.2)[attempt])          # FIXED, unjittered schedule
    old_oid = ref_lock._ref_oid(repo_root, LAST_PASS_REF, remote=remote) or _ZERO_OID
```

This loop is STALENESS-correct (it re-reads `old_oid` after the sleep, so the next CAS is against fresh state — unlike the baldish tickets-push bug). But the backoff schedule `(0.1, 0.2)` is deterministic and unjittered: two reconciler passes that collide once on LAST_PASS_REF sleep identical durations, wake together, and re-collide — the same thundering-herd/lockstep class as the JITTER half of baldish.

## Scope / why not fixed in the baldish change

This is a DIFFERENT subsystem (the reconciler ref-lock publication) with its own concurrency model — reconciler passes are more serialized than tickets writes, so the exposure is lower and the fix warrants its own review rather than being folded into the tickets-push bugfix. The staleness half does NOT apply here (the loop already re-reads after the sleep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The last-pass CAS publication backoff is jittered (additive jitter on the base schedule) so colliding reconciler passes do not wake in lockstep, mirroring the additive-jitter idiom now used by the tickets-push `_cas_backoff` (`src/rebar/_store/push_classify.py`) and the Jira DC transport.
- [ ] The staleness-correct re-read of `old_oid` after the sleep is preserved.
- [ ] A test drives colliding publications and asserts the backoff delays vary (not a single lockstep value), with a negative control at zero contention.

## Notes on adjacent non-siblings (from the same sweep, recorded so they are not re-triaged)

- `_TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_SECONDS` (push_classify.py) rides out a transient TLS fault, not writer contention — thundering-herd does not apply, jitter would not help convergence.
- `_coordinated_fetch`'s `_FETCH_CAS_BACKOFF_S` (sync.py) re-fetches after the sleep (staleness-correct) and serializes rebar peers behind `fetch_coordination_lock`, so rebar-peer lockstep is already prevented; the residual racer is a non-rebar git peer.
